def-confidence-set-and-coverage:
## Definition

Let \(\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})\) be a
statistical experiment as in [[def-statistical-experiment]], and assume
\(\Theta\ne\varnothing\). A **confidence-set procedure** is a map
\(C:\mathcal X\to\mathcal P(\Theta)\), where
\(\mathcal P(\Theta):=\{A:A\subseteq\Theta\}\), such that, for every
\(\eta\in\Theta\), its
membership section
$$C_\eta:=\{x\in\mathcal X:\eta\in C(x)\}$$
belongs to \(\mathcal A\). Its **coverage at \(\theta\)** is
\(c_C(\theta):=P_\theta(C_\theta)\), and its **confidence level** is
\(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}c_C(\theta)\), the greatest lower bound of those
coverage values. For \(0\le\alpha\le1\), it has coverage
at least \(1-\alpha\) if \(P_\theta(C_\theta)\ge1-\alpha\) for every
\(\theta\in\Theta\).

Only membership sections need to be measurable; no sigma-algebra on the
parameter set is assumed. The parameter is fixed in the repeated-sampling
coverage probability.
def-pivot:
## Definition

Let \(\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})\) be a
statistical experiment with \(\Theta\ne\varnothing\), and let
\((S,\mathcal S)\) be a measurable space. A
family of measurable maps \(q_\theta:\mathcal X\to S\), one for each
\(\theta\in\Theta\), is a **pivot** if the pushforward law
$$\nu_\theta(B):=P_\theta(q_\theta^{-1}(B)),\qquad B\in\mathcal S$$
is the same probability measure \(\nu\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
Each section is a random element on \((\mathcal X,\mathcal A,P_\theta)\), so
its pushforward is a probability measure by
[[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]].
No measurability in \(\theta\) is asserted or needed.

For \(S=\mathbb R\), a pivot is a real-valued statistic whose sampling
distribution is parameter-free. A pivot need not be invertible in the
parameter, and its inversion need not be an interval.
thm-pivot-inversion-exact-coverage:
## Statement

Let \(\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})\) be an
experiment with nonempty \(\Theta\). Let \(q_\theta:\mathcal X\to S\) be a
pivot with common law \(\nu\), and let \(B\in\mathcal S\). Define
$$C(x):=\{\theta\in\Theta:q_\theta(x)\in B\}$$
If \(\nu(B)\ge1-\alpha\), then \(C\) is a confidence set with coverage at
least \(1-\alpha\). If \(\nu(B)=1-\alpha\), its coverage is exactly
\(1-\alpha\) for every parameter value. For an interval \(B=[a,b]\) in
\(\mathbb R\), exactness requires calibration of the actual probability
\(\nu([a,b])\); quantile labels alone do not remove endpoint atoms.
thm-test-inversion-coverage:
## Statement

Let \(\mathsf E=((\mathcal Y,\mathcal G),(Q_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})\) be an
experiment with nonempty \(\Theta\), and let \(0\le\alpha\le1\). For each
\(\eta\in\Theta\), let \(A_\eta\in\mathcal G\) be the acceptance event of a
test of the point null \(\theta=\eta\), on the full observation space,
including any auxiliary randomization. Suppose
\(Q_\eta(A_\eta)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(\eta\in\Theta\).
Then \(C(y):=\{\eta\in\Theta:y\in A_\eta\}\)
is a confidence set with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).

The probability bound is the point-null level condition written in terms of
acceptance events. For a randomized test, a rejection-probability function on
the original data space is not itself an acceptance event; the auxiliary
randomization must be part of the observation before applying this statement.
